info.title: Signal Trade App API
info.description:
Public API for Signal Trade App — futures trade copier platform.

## What problems does this API solve?
- **Eliminates integration complexity** — Tradovate's native API requires OAuth 2.0 flows, WebSocket session management, rate-limit handling, and protobuf-level message parsing. SignalTradeApp abstracts all of that into clean REST endpoints and persistent WebSocket connections so you can place trades, read positions, and manage accounts with a single API key.
- **Trade copying at scale** — Manually mirroring orders across multiple accounts via Tradovate's API means building your own pub/sub engine, concurrency handling, and failure retry logic. Our API does this out of the box: one leader order propagates to every follower account in milliseconds.
- **Built-in risk guardrails** — Instead of writing your own Daily Loss Limit (DLL) or Daily Profit Trigger (DPT) logic, our API applies these protections broker-side automatically.

## SignalTradeApp vs. Tradovate Direct Integration
| | Tradovate Direct | SignalTradeApp API |
|---|---|---|
| Authentication | OAuth 2.0 + token refresh loops | Single X-API-Key header |
| Connection | DIY WebSocket reconnection & heartbeat | Managed, always-on WebSocket layer |
| Multi-account | Custom orchestration per account | One call copies to any group of accounts |
| Rate limits | Strict per-endpoint quotas | Aggregated, smart-routed to stay within broker limits |
| Trade execution | REST or WebSocket order entry | Unified REST API over managed broker WebSockets |

## Important notes
- **Market data is not available** on this API. Quote and candle endpoints are disabled. Use your broker's data feed or a market-data provider for prices.
- **Strategies are in beta.** The `/strategies` endpoints let you create and evaluate simple rules, but they do not auto-trade unless explicitly wired to an execution target.
- **Idempotency** is supported on `POST /accounts/{id}/orders`. Pass a unique `Idempotency-Key` header (8–128 chars) to safely retry requests. Cached responses are retained for 24 hours.
- **MCP (AI assistants).** `POST /api/mcp` is a read-only MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other MCP clients. Authenticate with the same API key (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`). Its tools read accounts, positions, orders, fills, risk, daily P&L, groups, connections and recent copies; none can place, change or cancel an order.
- **Demo accounts recommended for development.** Tradovate demo connections use the same order path as live accounts, making them the safest way to test trade-scoped integrations before risking real capital.

## Lightning-fast execution
- **Sub-100ms copy latency** via native WebSocket pub/sub (not polling).
- **Co-located infrastructure** with proximity to Tradovate and Rithmic matching engines.
- **No intermediary hops** — orders flow straight from our WebSocket layer to the broker's gateway; many competing platforms add a REST translation layer or queue that adds 200–500 ms.
- **Automatic failover** — if a broker connection drops, we reconnect and retry in the background without dropping your order.

Most competing trade-copier platforms rely on periodic REST polling or third-party bridges, introducing latency and missed fills. SignalTradeApp keeps a persistent, low-level WebSocket pipe open to each broker so your orders hit the market as fast as technically possible.

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description: Account, position, and trade history operations

price.description: Required for Limit and Stop orders

timeInForce.description: How long the bracket legs (and a Limit/Stop entry) rest. Omitted = Day: they expire at the session close, so a position held overnight loses its protection. GTC rests until filled or cancelled. Ignored for the entry of a Market order. If your account does not accept GTC (some prop firms refuse it) the order is rejected with the broker's reason — it is never downgraded to Day.

symbol.description: Symbol of the open position to protect

qty.description: Defaults to the full open position size

takeProfit.description: Set to null to clear existing TP

stopLoss.description: Set to null to clear existing SL

timeInForce.description: Applies to both legs. Omitted on a replace = keep what the live protection already has (GTC stays GTC); omitted with no protection live = Day, which expires at the session close. Moving a leg with PUT /accounts/{id}/orders/{orderId} also keeps its timeInForce. A refusal of GTC is returned as an error, never downgraded to Day.

ExpectedPosition.description: Only act if the position is still this one. Compared with the live position (the same side/qty/avgPrice that GET /stream sends); if it differs the request is refused with 409 POSITION_CHANGED and nothing is sent to the broker. Include avgPrice: it is what tells your position A apart from a B of the same side and size that opened after A exited.

get.description: Each account carries `balance` and `dayPnl`: today's realized P&L, **net of commissions** — the Day P&L the app shows. Open P&L is not included (see `GET /accounts/{id}/positions` or the stream). `tradingDay` is the CME trading day it belongs to, which rolls at 17:00 America/New_York; for Tradovate the broker's own trade date is used.

delete.summary: Flatten all positions on an account

403.description: API key missing trade scope or account inactive

get.summary: Risk limits and remaining drawdown for an account
get.description:
`drawdown` is what an account can still lose before it is liquidated, for sizing positions from what is left.

- `equity` — balance plus open P&L.
- `liquidationLevel` — the equity at which the account is liquidated.
- `drawdownRemaining` — `equity - liquidationLevel`. Negative means the line has been crossed.
- `drawdownType` — `STATIC`, `TRAILING` (real-time) or `EOD_TRAILING`; null when the broker does not say.
- `source` — `broker` when the broker reports the rule (Rithmic RMS, Tradovate prop-account auto-liquidation), `configured` when it comes from the drawdown the account owner entered on the Risk page, null when neither is known (all values null).

`profitToPass` is how far the account is from passing an evaluation: `targetBalance - equity`, where `targetBalance` is the start balance plus the profit target the account owner entered on the Risk page. Zero or negative means the target is reached. Null when no target is set; no broker reports one.

`brokerRms` is the raw Rithmic RMS block, kept for existing clients. Its `autoLiqThresholdCurrentValue` is a balance level, not headroom.

Returns executed trades for the account. This endpoint is named `/orders` for backwards compatibility.

**P&L fields:** `pnl` and `gross` are GROSS (price difference × quantity × point value). `fees` is the broker commission for the trade (entry + exit, or entry only while open) and `net` = `gross` − `fees`. Sum `net` by trading day to match the app's Day P&L and calendar.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Unique key for idempotent retries. Cached for 24 hours.

403.description: API key missing trade scope or account inactive

422.description: BROKER_ORDER_REJECTED — the broker refused the order; the message carries its reason. Terminal: do not retry without changing the request. (Returned 502 before this change.)

502.description: Broker did not return an order ID; the order may or may not be working — check GET /working-orders before retrying

get.description:
Every execution on your accounts as the broker reported it, oldest first: our `accountId`, `brokerAccountId` (the broker's account number), `id` (stable fill id, unique per account), `brokerFillId`, `orderId`, `symbol` (contract), `side`/`action`, `qty`, `price` (this execution's own price, not the order average), `fees` (USD, all broker fees on that fill) and `timestamp`.

**Live + catch-up:** each fill also arrives as a `fill` event on GET /stream with the same `id`. Keep the `cursor` of the last row you processed and call `/fills?after=<cursor>` when you reconnect to get everything you missed; deduplicate by `accountId` + `id`. Fills made while our connection to the broker was down are recovered from the broker's history when it reconnects (Tradovate: same trading day).

**Fees and brokerFillId** are read from the broker's own records and appear within about 15 seconds of the fill (Tradovate); until then they are `null`. Rows are only updated to add them.

The ledger starts recording when your first API key exists.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Return fills after this cursor (from a previous response)

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Executed at or after this time

200.description: { data: Fill[], meta: { limit, nextCursor, hasMore } }

get.summary: Live working orders for an account
get.description: Orders currently resting on the broker's book — unfilled entries and active TP/SL legs. Unlike `GET /accounts/{id}/orders` (closed trade history), this reads the broker directly, so it is the endpoint to poll when deciding whether a pending order still needs cancelling.

put.description:
Moves one resting order to a new price, and optionally a new size, WITHOUT cancelling it first.

**This is how you move a stop to breakeven or run a trailing stop.** Doing it as cancel-then-place leaves the position with no stop at all between the two calls; this endpoint does not.

**How gap-free it is depends on the broker — check `replaced` in the response:**

- **Tradovate** reprices IN PLACE, with no unprotected window. `replaced` is absent. A plain resting order keeps its id, but **a bracket leg (the stop or take-profit of a bracket) does not**: about a second after the first move, Tradovate re-issues both legs under NEW ids at the same prices. The broker OCO link stays intact (a filled stop still cancels the take-profit). Re-read `GET /accounts/{id}/working-orders` before each move instead of caching the id.
- **Rithmic** has no in-place modify: a modify is a cancel plus a re-place at the protocol level, so the order comes back under a NEW id and there is a brief window with nothing resting. `replaced: true`. Re-read `GET /accounts/{id}/working-orders` instead of caching the id you sent.

**Size is preserved by default.** Send `price` alone and the order keeps its current quantity — a reprice never silently resizes. Send `qty` only when you actually mean to resize.

**Order type is preserved.** `orderType` is accepted, but the broker's own view of the order wins: a reprice can never turn a Stop into a Limit.

**Rejections** (e.g. a stop placed through the market) come back as `400` carrying the broker's own reason.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: Broker order ID. On Rithmic this changes after each modify — re-read it from working-orders.

price.description: The new price. For a Stop this is the trigger price.

qty.description: Optional. Omit to keep the order at its current size.

orderType.description: Optional. Ignored when the broker already knows the order's type.

200.description: Order modified. `replaced: true` means the broker re-placed it under a new id.

400.description: Broker rejected the new price/size, no price supplied, or the broker does not support modification

403.description: API key missing trade scope or account inactive

503.description: Broker connection unavailable or client not connected. Retryable.

delete.description:
Cancels one order by the `orderId` returned from `POST /accounts/{id}/orders`.

**Never flattens.** An open position is untouched no matter which order you cancel — including the last remaining protective leg, which leaves the position open and unprotected rather than closing it.

**Unfilled bracket entry:** cancelling the entry also removes its attached TP/SL legs. Cancel the entry id only.

**Filled bracket:** once the entry fills, the TP/SL legs are live protection on a real position and are cancelled by their own ids. Note that cancelling ONE leg re-places the surviving leg under a NEW order id, so do not cache leg ids across a leg cancel — re-read `GET /accounts/{id}/working-orders` afterwards.

**Racing a fill:** if the order fills or is otherwise no longer cancellable, the broker rejects the cancel and this returns `409 CANCEL_REJECTED` with the broker's reason. Treat 409 as terminal (stop retrying) and `503` as retryable. Re-cancelling an already-cancelled order returns 200.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: Broker order ID from the order placement response.

400.description: Broker does not support order cancellation

403.description: API key missing trade scope or account inactive

409.description: CANCEL_REJECTED — the broker refused the cancellation, typically because the order already filled or is unknown to it. Terminal: do not retry.

503.description: Broker connection unavailable or client not connected. Retryable.

post.summary: Apply or update TP/SL protection on a position
post.description:
Attaches or REPLACES the broker-native TP/SL protection on an open position.

**Replacement is total.** Whatever was protecting the position beforehand is cancelled first — including TP/SL legs the broker attached itself when you placed a bracket at entry, which no `/protect` call ever created. The call only succeeds once those old orders are confirmed gone, so a `201` means nothing stale is still working. If the old protection cannot be cancelled you get `409 PROTECTION_CANCEL_FAILED` and nothing new is placed — your original protection is still live and untouched.

**Omitting a leg keeps it.** Send only `stopLoss` to move the stop and leave the take-profit exactly where it is; its current level is read from the live order, so a leg you dragged by hand is not reset. Send `null` to remove a leg outright.

**`legs[].orderId` are real, cancellable broker order ids** — the ids those orders are resting under, which you can pass straight to `DELETE` or `PUT /accounts/{id}/orders/{orderId}`. `ocoGroupId` is an opaque grouping token, NOT an order id; never send it as one.

**Note that replacing protection issues new orders**, so every leg id changes on every call. Re-read them from the response or from `GET /accounts/{id}/working-orders`; do not cache them across calls.

**Moving a stop to breakeven or trailing it:** prefer `PUT /accounts/{id}/orders/{orderId}` on the stop itself. That reprices the existing order rather than replacing the pair, which on Tradovate means the position is never unprotected for even a moment.

**Delayed or retried requests:** send `expected` (side, qty, avgPrice of the position you mean). If the position has changed by the time the request runs — for example it exited on its own SL/TP and a new one opened — you get `409 POSITION_CHANGED` and nothing is cancelled or placed.

Holding overnight:** protection is Day unless you send `timeInForce: "GTC"` — Day legs expire at the session close and the position is then unprotected. `GET /accounts/{id}/working-orders` and `order` events on `/stream` report each order's `timeInForce`; on `/stream` a leg that left the book carries `brokerStatus` (`Expired`, `Canceled`, `Rejected`), so an expiry is distinguishable from a cancel.

409.description: POSITION_CHANGED (expected did not match; nothing sent) or another protection update in progress

post.summary: Close one symbol (optionally only if it is still the expected position)
post.description:
Closes the position in ONE symbol with a broker-sized close, then cancels that symbol's working orders. Other symbols are untouched (unlike `DELETE /accounts/{id}/positions`, which flattens everything).

**Delayed or retried closes:** send `expected`. If the position is no longer that one — it already exited, or a new position opened — you get `409 POSITION_CHANGED` and nothing is closed or cancelled. With two months of the symbol held, `expected` is refused `409 POSITION_AMBIGUOUS`; name the contract (e.g. MNQZ6). `503 POSITIONS_UNKNOWN` means positions have not loaded yet — nothing was sent, retry.

A `200` with an empty `closed` list means nothing was held (only without `expected`).

403.description: API key missing trade scope or account inactive

409.description: POSITION_CHANGED or POSITION_AMBIGUOUS — nothing was sent

503.description: Broker not connected, or positions not loaded yet — nothing was sent

403.description: Market data is disabled for API consumers
Market data is disabled for API consumers

get.summary: Live orders, fills, positions, balances and drawdown
get.description:
Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream of everything that changes on your accounts. Use it instead of polling /accounts/{id}/positions and /accounts/{id}/orders.

The stream opens with a `snapshot` event (your accounts, `balances` with each account's balance and today's `dayPnl`, open positions, working orders and remaining drawdown), then sends:
- `order`: an order was placed, changed, filled, cancelled or rejected
- `fill`: an execution — same fields and same `id` as a row of GET /fills (fees and brokerFillId arrive via /fills ~15s later on Tradovate)
- `position`: a position changed (qty 0 means flat); at most once per second per account+symbol, latest value wins
- `balance`: balance, open P&L or today's realized P&L changed; at most once per second per account. `realizedPnl` is the broker's own figure: net of commissions on Tradovate, gross on Rithmic. `dayPnl` in the snapshot and on GET /accounts is always net
- `risk`: trailing/remaining drawdown changed — equity, liquidation level, drawdown remaining, profit to pass (the Risk page's numbers; sent when a value moves by $1 or more, at most once per second)
- `risk_settings`: risk limits were saved (same fields as GET /accounts/{id}/risk)
- `lock`: the account was locked or unlocked, including when a lock's time runs out
- `connection`: a broker connection changed status
- `heartbeat`: every 15 seconds

Every event carries our `accountId`, the same id the REST endpoints use. Pass `?accountId=` to receive one account only. Up to 5 streams can be open per user (across all your accounts); a sixth returns 429 TOO_MANY_STREAMS. If the stream drops (no event for 30 seconds), reconnect: the new snapshot brings you up to date.

Example:
```
data: {"type":"snapshot","accounts":[{"id":"acc_123","name":"DEMO1623501","status":"ACTIVE"}],"balances":[{"accountId":"acc_123","balance":50349.44,"dayPnl":349.44,"tradingDay":"2026-10-06"}],"positions":[],"orders":[],"ts":1719861123456}

data: {"type":"fill","id":"616507970099","orderId":"616507970052","accountId":"acc_123","symbol":"MNQZ6","side":"LONG","qty":1,"price":21440,"timestamp":"2024-07-01T19:12:05.000Z","ts":1719861125000}

data: {"type":"position","accountId":"acc_123","symbol":"MNQZ6","side":"LONG","qty":1,"avgPrice":21440,"openPnl":0,"ts":1719861125100}
```

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: Only send events for this account

404.description: accountId is not one of yours

get.description:
Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream for connection status changes.

Subscribe to this endpoint to receive real-time events when any of your broker connections:
- connect (CONNECTED)
- disconnect (RECONNECTING)
- reconnect (CONNECTED)
- hit an OAuth expiry (AUTH_EXPIRED)
- encounter a fatal error (ERROR)

Events are delivered as SSE data lines. The stream opens with a heartbeat, then sends a snapshot of every connection's current status, then emits status changes as they happen.

A heartbeat is sent every 15 seconds to keep the connection alive through proxies. The stream has no fixed lifetime — it stays open until the client closes it or the server restarts. Treat a gap of more than 30 seconds with no event of any kind as a dropped stream and reconnect.

Example event stream:
```
data: {"type":"snapshot","connectionId":"conn_abc","status":"CONNECTED","ts":1719861123456}

data: {"type":"status","connectionId":"conn_abc","status":"RECONNECTING","ts":1719861200000}

data: {"type":"heartbeat","ts":1719861240000}
```
Each group with its leader account and every follower: copyRatio, following (false = paused), inverseCopy, copyDelaySeconds and per-instrument symbolRules.

Every broker connection with status (CONNECTED, RECONNECTING, AUTH_EXPIRED, ERROR, DISCONNECTED, DISABLED), the error message when it is down, and how many accounts it carries. The live version is GET /connection-health/stream.
Per futures trading day (6PM–5PM ET): the total across accounts and one row per account. Defaults to the last 30 days; at most 366 days per request.
The last copy attempts (leader → follower, symbol, qty, success or failed, latency) within 24 hours, newest first. At most 10, and emptied when the server restarts.
